Yes, timing matters. Research suggests that the duration and timing of urban exposure are associated with the risk of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in Thailand. 

Studies have shown that people who moved to urban areas at a younger age or spent more time living in urban environments tend to have a higher risk of developing NCDs, such as obesity, diabetes, and hypertension, compared to those who moved at an older age or spent less time in urban areas.

This is likely due to the adoption of unhealthy lifestyles, including poor diet and physical inactivity, which are more prevalent in urban environments. Additionally, urbanization is often associated with increased exposure to air pollution, noise, and other environmental stressors that can contribute to NCD risk.

Therefore, the timing of urban exposure, including the age at which individuals move to urban areas and the duration of their stay, can play a significant role in shaping their risk of developing NCDs in Thailand.
